transcript: Theater is so back. I just saw Black Swan at the American Repertory Theatre up in Cambridge, Massachusetts. and y'all, it was insane! (Complimentary) Now, I've never seen the movie, so I have nothing to compare it to, but just based on what I've seen, I do think that Sonya Tayeh was the perfect choice to helm this material. It is billed as a dance thriller, and that's honestly exactly what it is. It's a very dance and movement focused show. And I think that her choreography is definitely the highlight here. The way that she is able to blend classical ballet with contemporary dance and yet make it feel so cohesive and natural is really stunning. She also incorporates a lot of, like, bird movements into the choreography, which I thought was genius. And she proves herself to be a really competent director as well, creating some really striking and, yes, at times horrifying imagery. And let's talk about the horror elements, because I did not find this show scary. There's no jump scares. There's a little bit of blood, but it's not gratuitous. There are a handful of moments of body horror, but for the most part, the horror is actually coming from the tension. Because, again, as the title says, this is a thriller. And the tension is constantly being dialed up to 11 over the course of the show as you watch this ballerina slowly descend more and more into madness. And I wanna take this moment To shout out Melanie Moore, who plays our main ballerina of Nina. Her performance in this show, I think, is going to be one of those performances that is talked about for years to come. And quite frankly, I don't know how she does this eight shows a week. It is such a demanding role, both physically and emotionally, and she is contorting her body in ways that I did not even know were possible. All of the performances in the show are really great, but she is definitely the standout. As for the show itself, I think it's in really good shape. There's definitely some refining that can be done. It can be tightened up a little bit. Certain things, I think, could be made clearer, particularly when it comes to the motivations of some of the side characters. But I was really taken with the score by Dave Malloy. I am a massive Dave Malloy fan, and this score feels so classic Dave Malloy. So I will say, if you're not a big fan of Dave Malloy’s style, I don't know that you're gonna love this show. There's a lot of the classic Dave Malloy talk singing in a vague melody, which, again, I didn't mind. I think it works. But I get why some people don't like it. If I'm being critical, I do think there are some points where the lyrics could be refined, moving away from some of the more obvious rhymes. And there are A handful of songs that tend to just kind of end with no real resolution, but all very easy to fix. And the music is absolutely gorgeous and is also helping to build that tension and keep you on the edge of your seat. I feel like we get a lot of really safe musicals these days, and so I love when a show is not afraid to take a big swing. And this is definitely a big swing. And it may not be a home run, but it's definitely like a triple. Is that when you make it to third base? I don't know sports, but it mostly lands. And I think with some refinement and fine tuning, it could be something really special. And so Black Swan is getting a Broadway Ben recommendation.
reasoning: Clear recommendation with enthusiasm for choreography, lead performance, and score, but explicit caveats about refinement needed, unclear side character motivations, and lyric issues. The 'triple, not a home run' framing signals strong positive but not rave.
